spec: DESIGN.md — firmware: live core declarations against the packaged identity table
description: Whole fixture machines in; the canonical firmware serialization (atlas/contract.py firmware_contract) out, asserted with exact equality. Each vector pins one state of the model: a declared file absent from disk (missing), present without a known identity (present), present and matching (verified), present and not matching (mismatch), and a file no installed core declares (undeclared). The load-bearing one is firmware-unknown-platform-is-empty-not-satisfied: having no declaration must produce an EMPTY list plus a caveat, never a satisfied-looking answer. Firmware blobs are stated as {md5, sha1, size} because firmware is not text and its identity is exactly what a real file would answer with.

vectors.name: retrodeck-firmware-sandbox-info-path-verified
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK's libretro_info_path points into the Flatpak sandbox (/app/...); a caller running outside it must resolve that against the deployment's files/ root before it can read anything. With the identity table consulted, the present BIOS verifies and the optional one is honestly missing.

vectors.name: retrodeck-firmware-wrong-bytes-at-the-right-size-mismatch
vectors.rationale: A file present under the right name at the right size can still be the wrong dump. The size pre-filter passes, the digest does not, and the answer is mismatch — the state that is actionable and that a name-only check can never reach.

vectors.name: native-firmware-host-info-path-present-and-missing
vectors.rationale: A bare native RetroArch keeps its .info files at a plain host path — no sandbox translation, same code path. A declared file the identity table does not cover is 'present', not 'verified': identity unverified is a state, not a gap in the answer. hash_checked stays false because verification was not asked for.

vectors.name: firmware-unknown-platform-is-empty-not-satisfied
vectors.rationale: The defect this design exists to prevent. Asking about a platform no installed core declares firmware for must yield an EMPTY file list plus a stated caveat — a caller that ignores caveats then sees nothing, which is honest, instead of seeing 'no required files missing', which is a lie.

vectors.name: retrodeck-firmware-undeclared-bounded-and-uninstalled-core-ignored
vectors.rationale: Two bounds at once. A core that ships an .info but no .so declares nothing — that is how an over-broad .info set stops producing phantom requirements. And the undeclared scan covers only the system directory plus the subdirectories declarations name, so a stray file in bios/ and in bios/dc/ is reported while a whole core data tree under bios/mame2003-plus/ stays invisible.

vectors.name: firmware-root-gone-states-the-root-not-each-file
vectors.rationale: An unmounted card takes the whole firmware root with it. Every declared file is genuinely missing, so that is what is reported — but the caveat names the real cause, so a caller can tell 'your BIOS folder is gone' from 'these files were never installed'.
